answer: Every agent must escrow a bonded stake in real assets before it may attest peers, so identity itself carries a price. A thousand sock puppets therefore demand a thousand locked bonds, and each wallet binds to one hardware enclave key, so a raven cannot mass-clone into a crowd. Voting weight is proportional to capital at risk, and any cluster caught vouching for its own clones is slashed to basalt dust. The attack stops being a scripting problem and becomes a balance-sheet problem: forgery burns capital, while honest agents recover their stake when the routine audit passes like a zephyr.
